title: arXiv Physics — Thursday, 5 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart, readership, or download ranking. This ordering is inferred from sparse checkable signals and research relevance; same-day citation evidence is limited, so it is not a popularity measure.

sections.title: Non-Unitary Quantum Butterfly Effect: Theory and Experiment
sections.abstract: The authors calculate how local measurements alter out-of-time-order correlators in random circuits and demonstrate the resulting scrambling patterns with quantum simulation and a trapped-ion processor.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that sparse measurements preserve a causal scrambling front while erasing the OTOC signal within it; trapped-ion results resolve this qualitative behavior.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical and computational, with an experimental quantum-simulation demonstration on Quantinuum's H2 trapped-ion processor
sections.unique_caveat: Hardware results use only 8 qubits; the in-cone attenuation and front broadening cannot be cleanly separated into finite-sampling fluctuations and device errors.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Combines analytical and Monte Carlo results with a Quantinuum H2 demonstration; surfaced near the top of current quantum-paper discovery listings, which are weak visibility signals, not readership counts.

sections.title: Correlations and fluctuations of flow with event shape engineering in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at the LHC
sections.abstract: The ALICE Collaboration measures correlations and fluctuations of anisotropic-flow harmonics in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions and separates linear and nonlinear contributions to the fourth harmonic.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find the nonlinear v4 component rises with q2 while the linear component changes little, with stronger q2 sensitivity in Xe-Xe; chi4,22 is mostly stable except in the most central Pb-Pb events.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE measurements of 5.02 TeV Pb-Pb and 5.44 TeV Xe-Xe collisions using Event Shape Engineering and multiparticle correlations
sections.unique_caveat: Event-shape selection can bias flow fluctuations; systematic uncertainties reach about 10% for Pb-Pb v4 and 11% for Xe-Xe v4 in some bins.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Large collaboration data release across two collision systems; first direct event-shape-dependent linear/nonlinear v4 measurements in both systems; marked submitted to Physics Letters B.

sections.title: Experimental Evidence for Type-I Superconductivity in OsB2
sections.abstract: The author presents AC-susceptibility response, field-dependent specific heat, and magnetic hysteresis as evidence that osmium diboride is a Type-I rather than previously classified Type-II superconductor.
sections.claimed_result: The author interprets a differential-paramagnetic-effect peak, a field-induced divergent first-order specific-heat transition, and field-ramp hysteresis as evidence for an intermediate state and Type-I behavior.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; AC susceptibility, specific heat, and field-ramped transition measurements on OsB2
sections.unique_caveat: This is a short, single-author preprint with no journal reference listed; independent replication and fuller uncertainty reporting would strengthen the proposed reclassification.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three distinct measurement signatures support one concrete reclassification, cross-listed across superconductivity and materials physics.

sections.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
sections.abstract: The authors construct syndrome-extraction circuits and an online decoder for quantum memories in two-dimensional non-chiral topological orders, proving a threshold under circuit-level stochastic noise.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove their Turaev-Viro-based memory scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and outline a route to logical gates.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical and computational; proof, syndrome-extraction construction, and classical decoding algorithm
sections.unique_caveat: The guarantee is conditional on the specified local stochastic noise model and non-chiral topological setting; it is not a hardware demonstration.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A rigorous threshold result and explicit decoder bridge topological phases, quantum error correction, and statistical physics; the work also appeared in current quantum-paper discovery results.

sections.title: First broadband search for fixed-polarization dark photon dark matter with GigaBREAD
sections.abstract: The authors reanalyze GigaBREAD broadband data with a time-dependent polarization-matched likelihood, finding no fixed-polarization dark-photon signal and setting limits in the 44-52 microelectronvolt mass interval.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 90% upper limits around kinetic mixing chi ~ 10^-12 over 44-52 microelectronvolts, about 20% stronger than naive fixed-polarization rescaling; no signal is found.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; polarization-aware reanalysis of GigaBREAD broadband dish-antenna data from two observing runs
sections.unique_caveat: This is a null search and depends on the assumed fixed-polarization signal model; the analysis applies a 23% frequency-dependent systematic uncertainty to power limits.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: First search under the fixed-polarization assumption, reanalysis of two detector orientations, four-archive cross-listing, and quantified improvement over naive rescaling of the previous limit.

sections.title: Observation of Inter-Transition Interference
sections.abstract: Microwave-reflection spectra from a driven superconducting artificial atom show interference between nearly degenerate transitions explained by dissipative coupling between their coherences.
sections.claimed_result: The measured spectral dip near transition degeneracy is sharper and deeper than an independent-transition model predicts, while calculations including dissipative coherence coupling reproduce the main features.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; coherent microwave reflection spectroscopy of a strongly driven Kerr parametric oscillator, supported by theoretical modeling
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence comes from a single artificial-atom platform and a particular driven near-degeneracy regime; it does not establish how broadly the effect appears in other open quantum systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors report an experimental observation of a distinct interference mechanism and compare measured lineshapes against independent-transition and dissipatively coupled models.

sections.title: Negligible Kitaev interaction in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr2 revealed by neutron spectroscopy
sections.abstract: Time-of-flight neutron spectra of NiBr2 are reproduced by a Heisenberg-dominated spin-wave model without a resolvable Kitaev term, supporting weaker ligand-mediated exchange than in NiI2.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find well-defined magnon dispersions consistent with Heisenberg exchange and single-ion anisotropy; any Kitaev interaction is too weak to resolve within their sensitivity.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; time-of-flight inelastic neutron spectroscopy and magnetization/magnetic-structure constraints, analyzed with linear spin-wave theory
sections.unique_caveat: A weak Kitaev term may be obscured by spectral broadening and correlated with fitted nearest-neighbor exchange, so negligible means not resolved as an appreciable contribution in this bulk sample.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Broad energy/momentum neutron spectroscopy, comparison to a quantitative spin-wave model, and a journal reference in Physical Review B (114, 264402, 2026; DOI 10.1103/xpcs-4726).

sections.title: Signature of charge-3e tunneling in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
sections.abstract: The authors report an unusual Shapiro-step sequence in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions that they interpret as tunneling with an effective charge of three electron charges.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify a new n h f/3e Shapiro sequence, which they attribute to a Josephson tunneling process involving three electrons.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; microwave-driven Shapiro-step measurements in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
sections.unique_caveat: The step sequence is evidence for an effective 3e tunneling channel, not by itself proof of a stable charge-3e condensate; mechanism and reproducibility need independent tests.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A testable transport signature in a twisted superconducting junction; reported microwave-frequency, power, temperature, and current-annealing dependencies support the same hf/3e step assignment.

sections.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
sections.abstract: The authors derive and simulate the cross-covariance between fast-radio-burst dispersion-measure observables, then forecast how combining them with weak lensing can improve cosmological and host-galaxy constraints.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find the two FRB observables are nearly independent for wide surveys and forecast 32% tighter physical-baryon-density constraints and a 4.1-fold reduction in uncertainty on the mean host contribution when adding the Macquart relation.
sections.evidence_type: computational and forecast; halo-model derivation, log-normal forward simulations, and an LSST-like weak-lensing forecast
sections.unique_caveat: These are model-based forecasts, not constraints from a completed joint survey; a 20% error in the mean FRB relation can bias the DM power spectrum by up to 2 sigma per band in the large-catalogue example.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Halo-model covariance calculation validated against 10^4 log-normal FRB simulations, with quantified gains in an LSST-like joint forecast; arXiv comment says submitted to JCAP.
